Longitudinal Summary

Across 2H 2023 into 2024, management positioned revenue growth as resilient but modest, citing core organic revenue growth near ~1% and expecting improving quarterly trends through the year. In Q3 2023, multiple FY2024 framing statements were met (including guidance that FY2024 core organic growth would be ~similar to 2023). In Q4 2023, the full-year 2024 organic revenue range guidance was partially missed on the “minus 1% to positive 1%” framing (per the verdict), though the company indicated improving sequential quarters and reported results consistent with improvement in the second half. In 2024, Q2 showed better-than-previously-assumed performance (core organic growth “a little over 0.5 percentage point ahead”), while management maintained a rounded FY2024 range and provided higher Q3 modeling assumptions; Q3 2024 results were not provided in the evidence set, leaving that pair unresolved.

Forecasting Credibility: Medium

Out of 8 guidance/actual pairs with a verdict, management Met/Exceeded in 6 and Missed in 1, with 1 left Unresolved. This “mostly Met” pattern is consistent with credible forecasting for the revenue-growth trajectory, though at least one notable miss occurred around the FY2024 organic growth framing in Q4 2023. The unresolved item (Q3 2024 outcome) limits confidence in near-term precision, but the majority of resolved pairs were met.

Trends

  • Core organic revenue growth guided around ~1% with an improving quarterly cadence
  • Q2 2024 core organic growth outperformed the prior guide assumption by ~0.5 percentage point
  • COVID-19 related demand headwinds and China macro pressure repeatedly referenced as drivers of slower regional growth

Recurring Themes / Risks

  • COVID-19 product demand runoff
  • Challenging macroeconomic environment and low activity in China
  • Revenue growth sensitivity to organic demand vs. acquisitions (reported revenue includes acquisition contributions)
  • Guidance expressed as core organic growth (excluding acquisitions/divestitures and currency effects) to isolate underlying demand

Key Concerns

  • Q4 2023 guidance for FY2024 core organic revenue growth in the range of minus 1% to positive 1% is marked as a miss in the guidance/actual verdict set, indicating at least one period where the communicated range did not track the eventual outcome well (exact FY2024 result not provided in the excerpts).
  • One guidance item tied to “relative to the midpoint…model Q3…1% higher than we delivered in Q2” remains unresolved due to missing Q3 2024 outcome data in the provided evidence.
  • Acquisition-related contributions were explicitly assumed for reported revenue growth in Q3 2023, but the pair “~$300 million to reported revenue growth for the year” was marked missed, suggesting reported (as opposed to core organic) revenue forecasting incorporating deal impact was less reliable.

Conclusion

Revenue growth evolved from a modest, core-organic baseline (~1% core organic growth) with an expectation of sequential improvement in 2H 2023 into early/mid-2024 where management maintained the rounded FY2024 organic growth band while reporting better-than-expected Q2 organic performance. In Q3 2023, guidance that FY2024 core organic growth would be similar to 2023 (~1%) was met, and Q3 2023 also reported 1% core organic growth. In Q4 2023, the guidance framing for FY2024 core organic growth was assessed as missed in the pair verdict set, though management also guided for improvement each quarter and referenced market conditions playing out as expected. In Q2 2024, management reported core organic revenue growth “a little over 0.5 percentage point ahead” of the prior Q2 guide assumption (with the pair marked met), supporting that underlying demand trended better than expected at least by that point in the year.

And within the proteomics franchise, now with a successful Orbitrap franchise of last 15-plus years, combining that with the -- with Olink, Marc, maybe at a high level, could you provide us your, for lack of a better word, vision on proteomics despite being a sort of a tough market this year and next year?Q3 2023complete1Earnings transcripthighsource
Yeah. So, many thanks for the question. And so, when I think about the M&A for this year or M&A even in general, right, the criteria that we use, right, is M&A that's going to be highly valued by our customers, strengthen our strategic position, generate strong returns for our shareholders, right? And you look at what the different opportunities are and you think about in different periods of time where it's going to skew in your favor. And this year, with a more volatile macro, we've been able to add three phenomenal businesses, right, in terms of strengthening the company with incredible growth prospects, really good return profiles, right? So, that doesn't mean that next year will look exactly like this or years where you can buy companies that are really more of a balance of cost and revenue growth and those different things and different aspects of it. But this year, to be able to get The Binding Site, CorEvitas, and Olink, it's fantastic. And, Puneet, thanks for reminding others about our 15-year-plus track record of Orbitrap. Thanks. Good morning, guys. I wanted to start by asking about LSS. So this had some nice sequential improvement in the growth rate. I heard biosciences led the growth. Can you talk about the relative improvement you're seeing there, also genetic sciences and bioprocessing. And any updates on where you think your customers stand in terms of feedstock?Q2 2024complete1Earnings transcripthighsource
Sure, Jack. Thanks for the question. When I think about probably the most important points on our Life Science Solutions segment, nice to see the growth in our biosciences business. That's every lab every day, really nice adoption in the pharma and biotech segment there. So that was very -- a nice, positive development terms there. And maybe I'll dive a little bit into bioproduction, which is always an area of great interest to our investors. The business is actually progressing really exactly as we expected, really nice quarter of performance. So when I think about the most salient facts around bioproduction, sequentially, really nice revenue growth in Q2. When I look at orders, we had really nice sequential growth in orders. We had year-over-year growth in orders, and we had a favorable book-to-bill, so progressing well. And when I look at others that have reported, I feel very good about our performance. So when I think about the Life Science Solutions segment, those are two of the drivers. And then, you've seen some announcements in the previous few months about important companion diagnostics. Our clinical sequencing business is doing quite well. So Jack, thanks for the question on LSS.Q2 2024complete1Earnings transcripthighsource
Great. And then, just as a follow-up here. On the CRO, you called out clinical research was an outperformer this quarter that drove some of the growth. So we've seen a few volatile prints from your peers. So can you walk us through what have you seen from an RFP standpoint and book-to-bill in the quarter for PPD? And then, have we turned the quarter on emerging biotech funding and kind of how is that flowing through the model as well?Q2 2024complete1Earnings transcripthighsource
Yes. So Rachel, team has done a really nice job executing very well in our clinical research business. And when I think about our performance, we delivered positive organic revenue growth despite a really substantial headwind from the runoff of vaccines and therapies in that activity. So team is doing a nice job. Commercial execution was very strong in the quarter, right? And customers value our capabilities. And when I sort of went under the details of the commercial performance and looked at some of the underlying trends, it was very clear that in Q2, we really did see some of the biotech funding activity that we talked about is a green shoot in Q1 that would give us confidence that the year in aggregate across our business would be improving from a market perspective. We saw that in Q2 actually translate into an acceleration of authorizations in our biotech customer base. And that really does bode well for that. And as you know well this business, that really translates more into revenue in '25 and '26 in terms of how long it takes to get the clinical trials up and going, but the authorization momentum very encouraging in the quarter. Thank you, Rachel.Q2 2024complete1Earnings transcripthighsource

Q3 2023
View TranscriptView SEC filing

What management said

  • "A revised estimate for 2023 is revenue of $42.7 billion with core organic revenue growth of just under 1% and $21.50 of adjusted EPS."
  • "At this point in time, a good starting assumption is that our core organic revenue growth in 2024 is similar to 2023, approximately 1% growth."
  • "So, the high-level summary is that with these assumptions, we'd expect 2024 core organic revenue growth to be similar to 2023 and that our proven growth strategy and PPI business system would enable us to continue to manage the macro conditions and the runoff in pandemic revenue very effectively so we can deliver revenue and profitability similar to 2023 and a slight increase in adjusted EPS."
  • "In Q3, we delivered $10.6 billion of revenue, which included 1% core organic revenue growth; our PPI business system enabled us to generate 200 basis points of adjusted operating margin expansion; and we delivered $5.69 of adjusted EPS, a 12% increase over Q3 last year."
  • "The Binding Site and CorEvitas acquisitions are performing well, and we now assume that they'll contribute approximately $300 million to our reported revenue growth for the year."
  • "We expect the total vaccines- and therapies-related revenue will be $1.6 billion less than the prior year, an impact of over 4% on our core organic revenue growth."
  • "In the third quarter, our revenue was $10.57 billion, our adjusted operating income grew 8% to $2.56 billion, and we expanded our adjusted operating margin 200 basis points to 24.2%, and we delivered excellent growth in adjusted EPS, achieving a 12% increase to $5 and 69% -- $5.69 per share."
  • "In the analytical instruments segment, reported revenue increased 8% in Q3 and organic growth was also 8%."
  • "Finally, in the laboratory products and biopharma services segment, Q3 reported revenue increased 3% and organic growth was 1%."
  • "We expect this business to be a mid-teens revenue growth business for us well into the future."
  • "During Q3, organic revenue growth in this segment was led by the pharma services business."
  • "However, we continue to effectively navigate the macro dynamics and expect to continue to deliver differentiated core organic revenue growth for the year despite the more challenging conditions."
  • "In terms of phasing of our core organic revenue growth, it's best to assume a more challenging first half and then moderate growth in the second half."
  • "So, that doesn't mean that next year will look exactly like this or years where you can buy companies that are really more of a balance of cost and revenue growth and those different things and different aspects of it."
  • "And when we look to the future, you know, we expect this to be a long term, you know, mid-teens-plus growth business and be able to generate really significant, you know, adjusted operating income synergies, driven by that accelerated revenue growth."
8 guidance point(s)6 distinct actual(s)0 verified outcome(s)

What was asked

Q — Puneet Souda — Leerink Partners: Yeah. Thanks, Marc, for taking the questions. I'll wrap two of my questions into one. First, largely on M&A, given the environment right now, the type of deals that you're doing, the type of valuations you're doing at, could you maybe just give us a sense of what you're seeing out there? Obviously, Olink, prior to that, Binding Site and CorEvitas, is that the type of sort of mid-sized deals that we should continue to expect here and the opportunity base that you are seeing in M&A? And within the proteomics franchise, now with a successful Orbitrap franchise of last 15-plus years, combining that with the -- with Olink, Marc, maybe at a high level, could you provide us your, for lack of a better word, vision on proteomics despite being a sort of a tough market this year and next year?
A: Yeah. So, many thanks for the question. And so, when I think about the M&A for this year or M&A even in general, right, the criteria that we use, right, is M&A that's going to be highly valued by our customers, strengthen our strategic position, generate strong returns for our shareholders, right? And you look at what the different opportunities are and you think about in different periods of time where it's going to skew in your favor. And this year, with a more volatile macro, we've been able to add three phenomenal businesses, right, in terms of strengthening the company with incredible growth prospects, really good return profiles, right? So, that doesn't mean that next year will look exactly like this or years where you can buy companies that are really more of a balance of cost and revenue growth and those different things and different aspects of it. But this year, to be able to get The Binding Site, CorEvitas, and Olink, it's fantastic. And when I think about Olink, which this is our first opportunity, given that we had announced it during a blackout period, it's just a terrific fit, right? And you think about it's a leader in a business that has gone through that phase of being well adopted, right? So, the technology risk isn't here anymore. But it hasn't globally commercialized. It hasn't reached nearly its full potential and incredibly complementary to our leading position in mass spectrometry and proteomics. And, Puneet, thanks for reminding others about our 15-year-plus track record of Orbitrap. Astral being the next big many-year run, and the combination of AR plus Olink and the fact that we have a leading position in the life sciences instrumentation, which are very relevant in terms of qPCR for these products as well, really exciting. You know, they are a leader in their field, and we're excited to help bring that to the customer base in an accelerated fashion. And when we look to the future, you know, we expect this to be a long term, you know, mid-teens-plus growth business and be able to generate really significant, you know, adjusted operating income synergies, driven by that accelerated revenue growth. And on top of that, there's $125 million of earnings that come from the year 5 synergies, and that's going to generate double-digit returns for the shareholders. So, super exciting time, and we'll continue to be outstanding stewards of our shareholders' capital. Great. Thank you. Thanks.

What management said

  • "Core organic revenue growth was a little over 0.5 percentage point ahead of what we'd assumed in the prior guide for Q2."
  • "The improved revenue guidance does not change the core organic revenue growth rounding of the year, so we still continue to assume core organic revenue growth will be in the range of minus 1% to positive 1% for 2024."
  • "Relative to the midpoint of the guide, I recommend modeling Q3 organic revenue growth 1% higher than we delivered in Q2."
  • "This represents a 3% headwind to organic revenue growth."
  • "Also, good to model core organic revenue growth in Q3 1% higher than we delivered in Q2."
  • "In the Analytical Instruments segment, reported revenue grew 2%, and our organic growth was 3% higher than the prior year quarter."
  • "And finally, in the Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services segment, both reported revenue and organic growth decreased 1% in Q2 versus the prior year quarter."
  • "As a reminder, the reported growth in this end market is impacted by the runoff of COVID-19 testing-related revenue."
  • "And in Q2, core organic revenue growth rounded up to flat on a year-over-year basis."
  • "We delivered another strong sequential improvement in core organic revenue growth this quarter."
  • "During the quarter, the team delivered good core revenue growth, highlighted by our transplant diagnostics and immunodiagnostics businesses, as well as our healthcare market channel."
  • "So when I think about the most salient facts around bioproduction, sequentially, really nice revenue growth in Q2."
  • "And when I think about our performance, we delivered positive organic revenue growth despite a really substantial headwind from the runoff of vaccines and therapies in that activity."

What was asked

Q — Jack Meehan. Jack — your line is now open: Thanks. Good morning, guys. I wanted to start by asking about LSS. So this had some nice sequential improvement in the growth rate. I heard biosciences led the growth. Can you talk about the relative improvement you're seeing there, also genetic sciences and bioprocessing. And any updates on where you think your customers stand in terms of feedstock?
A: Sure, Jack. Thanks for the question. When I think about probably the most important points on our Life Science Solutions segment, nice to see the growth in our biosciences business. That's every lab every day, really nice adoption in the pharma and biotech segment there. So that was very -- a nice, positive development terms there. And maybe I'll dive a little bit into bioproduction, which is always an area of great interest to our investors. The business is actually progressing really exactly as we expected, really nice quarter of performance. So when I think about the most salient facts around bioproduction, sequentially, really nice revenue growth in Q2. When I look at orders, we had really nice sequential growth in orders. We had year-over-year growth in orders, and we had a favorable book-to-bill, so progressing well. And when I look at others that have reported, I feel very good about our performance. So when I think about the Life Science Solutions segment, those are two of the drivers. And then, you've seen some announcements in the previous few months about important companion diagnostics. Our clinical sequencing business is doing quite well. So Jack, thanks for the question on LSS.
Q — Rachel Vatnsdal — J.P: Great. And then, just as a follow-up here. On the CRO, you called out clinical research was an outperformer this quarter that drove some of the growth. So we've seen a few volatile prints from your peers. So can you walk us through what have you seen from an RFP standpoint and book-to-bill in the quarter for PPD? And then, have we turned the quarter on emerging biotech funding and kind of how is that flowing through the model as well?
A: Yes. So Rachel, team has done a really nice job executing very well in our clinical research business. And when I think about our performance, we delivered positive organic revenue growth despite a really substantial headwind from the runoff of vaccines and therapies in that activity. So team is doing a nice job. Commercial execution was very strong in the quarter, right? And customers value our capabilities. And when I sort of went under the details of the commercial performance and looked at some of the underlying trends, it was very clear that in Q2, we really did see some of the biotech funding activity that we talked about is a green shoot in Q1 that would give us confidence that the year in aggregate across our business would be improving from a market perspective. We saw that in Q2 actually translate into an acceleration of authorizations in our biotech customer base. And that really does bode well for that. And as you know well this business, that really translates more into revenue in '25 and '26 in terms of how long it takes to get the clinical trials up and going, but the authorization momentum very encouraging in the quarter. Thank you, Rachel.

TMO: Operating margin

Longitudinal Summary

Across 2023, GAAP operating margin benefited at quarter level from productivity and price realization, while also being pressured by lower COVID-19 related volumes and restructuring charges. In Q3 2023, management guided to an FY 2023 adjusted operating margin of 22.9% and later resolved that guidance as Exceeded in the Q4 2023 reporting, but other margin-related guidance in adjusted operating income dollars did not resolve in-line (Missed). In Q4 2023, the company reiterated FY 2023 adjusted operating margin of 22.9% as in line with prior guide, while Q4 2023 guidance for 2024 adjusted operating margin (22.3%–22.8%) was later missed. In 2024, GAAP and adjusted operating margins were described as improving early in the year due to productivity gains, but by Q2 2024 at least one adjusted operating margin measure was materially below the prior-year quarter, and full-year 2024 was described as decreasing on GAAP largely due to business mix and strategic investments (partially offset by lower amortization expense).

Forecasting Credibility: Medium

Out of 3 guidance/actual pairs with verdicts, management demonstrated credibility with 2 outcomes resolving as Exceeded (Q3 2023 FY adjusted operating margin 22.9%) and 1 outcome resolving as Missed (2024 adjusted operating margin range 22.3%–22.8%). One additional margin-related guidance point (Q1 slightly under 21%) is explicitly marked unresolved in the provided evidence, but it is not included in the 3-pair verdict count. Overall, the limited sample shows mixed precision across forward periods, with better accuracy for the FY 2023 adjusted margin than for the 2024 margin range.

Revenue & Operating Income trend
Revenue ($10.71B → $10.60B) Operating Income (% of revenue) (14.6% → 17.3%)
Q1 2023 – Q3 2024
▲ Operating Income turned up in Q2 2024

“And adjusted operating margin was 12.9%, which is 120 basis points lower than Q2 2023, flat sequentially to Q1 2024.”

Trends

  • GAAP operating income margin affected by lower COVID-19 volumes and restructuring charges in 2023
  • Productivity improvements and price realization supported adjusted operating margins in Q3 2023
  • FY 2023 adjusted operating margin target around 22.9% ultimately resolved higher than guided/expected within the pair framework
  • 2024 GAAP operating margin described as decreasing despite productivity gains, with lower amortization offsetting
  • Adjusted operating margin performance in 2024 shows internal variability by quarter/measure (e.g., Q2 below prior-year for one measure)

Recurring Themes / Risks

  • Revenue headwinds from COVID-19 related demand variability
  • Restructuring/facility consolidation charges impacting GAAP operating margin
  • Strategic investments and unfavorable business mix pressuring margins
  • Productivity improvements partially offsetting operational headwinds
  • Amortization expense levels (including lower amortization in 2024) affecting GAAP margin

Key Concerns

  • GAAP operating margin statements are repeatedly framed as being impacted by restructuring charges and fixed intangible amortization, making GAAP margin less comparable across periods versus adjusted margin.
  • The Q2 2024 evidence shows multiple adjusted operating margin figures (e.g., 12.9% and 24.6% and 22.3% and 26.7% in the transcript), which indicates sensitivity to how margin is defined/measured; this complicates interpretation of “operating margin” without a single consistent metric.
  • One Q1 2024 margin guidance point is marked Unresolved (slightly under 21%), limiting confidence in short-cycle margin forecasting based on the provided dataset.

Conclusion

Operating margin evolved from being pressured in 2023 by lower COVID-19 related revenue and restructuring/intangible amortization effects toward quarters where productivity and price realization improved margins (e.g., Q3 2023 GAAP operating income margin described as up due to productivity and price realization, partially offset by lower COVID-19 revenue). For adjusted operating margin, management guided to 22.9% for FY 2023 and the later reported outcome resolved as Exceeded within the guidance/actual pair framework, with GAAP operating income margin in Q3 2023 at 17.6% versus 16.0% and a full-year GAAP operating income margin of 16.0% versus 18.7% (filing). For 2024, the company guided adjusted operating income margins in a 22.3%–22.8% range, but that was resolved as Missed, and in 2024 the filing narrative indicates GAAP operating margin decreased due to unfavorable business mix and strategic investments, partially offset by lower amortization expense.

Yeah. Thanks, Marc, for taking the questions. I'll wrap two of my questions into one. First, largely on M&A, given the environment right now, the type of deals that you're doing, the type of valuations you're doing at, could you maybe just give us a sense of what you're seeing out there? Obviously, Olink, prior to that, Binding Site and CorEvitas, is that the type of sort of mid-sized deals that we should continue to expect here and the opportunity base that you are seeing in M&A? And within the proteomics franchise, now with a successful Orbitrap franchise of last 15-plus years, combining that with the -- with Olink, Marc, maybe at a high level, could you provide us your, for lack of a better word, vision on proteomics despite being a sort of a tough market this year and next year?Q3 2023complete1Earnings transcripthighsource
Yeah. So, many thanks for the question. And so, when I think about the M&A for this year or M&A even in general, right, the criteria that we use, right, is M&A that's going to be highly valued by our customers, strengthen our strategic position, generate strong returns for our shareholders, right? And you look at what the different opportunities are and you think about in different periods of time where it's going to skew in your favor. And this year, with a more volatile macro, we've been able to add three phenomenal businesses, right, in terms of strengthening the company with incredible growth prospects, really good return profiles, right? So, that doesn't mean that next year will look exactly like this or years where you can buy companies that are really more of a balance of cost and revenue growth and those different things and different aspects of it. But this year, to be able to get The Binding Site, CorEvitas, and Olink, it's fantastic. And when I think about Olink, which this is our first opportunity, given that we had announced it during a blackout period, it's just a terrific fit, right? And you think about it's a leader in a business that has gone through that phase of being well adopted, right? So, the technology risk isn't here anymore. But it hasn't globally commercialized. It hasn't reached nearly its full potential and incredibly complementary to our leading position in mass spectrometry and proteomics. And, Puneet, thanks for reminding others about our 15-year-plus track record of Orbitrap. Astral being the next big many-year run, and the combination of AR plus Olink and the fact that we have a leading position in the life sciences instrumentation, which are very relevant in terms of qPCR for these products as well, really exciting. You know, they are a leader in their field, and we're excited to help bring that to the customer base in an accelerated fashion. And when we look to the future, you know, we expect this to be a long term, you know, mid-teens-plus growth business and be able to generate really significant, you know, adjusted operating income synergies, driven by that accelerated revenue growth. And on top of that, there's $125 million of earnings that come from the year 5 synergies, and that's going to generate double-digit returns for the shareholders. So, super exciting time, and we'll continue to be outstanding stewards of our shareholders' capital.Q3 2023complete1Earnings transcripthighsource
Hi there. Good morning and thanks a lot for the question. I'd love to ask about your lab products and biopharma services business unit. So, the operating margin there was a bright spot at 16%. It was higher than any point in the past. And when you talked about the puts and takes there, you called out productivity and mix as some of the positive drivers. So, just two questions there. One, on mix, if that was a positive driver, does that actually mean that sales of some of your really low-margin consumables were down? Other peer companies have talked about challenges there and brought down guidance in general lab products. So, can you talk a little bit about those dynamics? And then secondly, on productivity gains, what is driving that and are those going to be sustainable and recurring over time?Q3 2023complete1Earnings transcripthighsource
Yeah. So, Eve, thanks for the question. So, when I think about the margin dynamic in that segment, yeah, mix is -- it -- when you think about where the more challenging environment is in terms of customer caution and China, that impacts the lab products business, and then the wider customer caution also impacts our channel business. So, relative to the other business in that segment, that's where the mix profile comes from. In terms of productivity is about we've been rightsizing the cost base within our lab products business and given the volume change. So, that's where the majority of that is. And then just, you know, good spending wisely across the whole business. But those are probably the two main factors to call out.Q3 2023complete1Earnings transcripthighsource

Thanks. Marc, a question on operating margins or maybe for Stephen. Lab products and services, obviously, you felt the headwinds from the vaccine and therapy roll off, but it was effectively at a two-year low. So just curious about how you think about margin for lab products going forward? And then, as we think about 2025, if TPD and Patheon can grow above the corporate average, do you still have the ability to drive 40 to 50 bps of margin expansion or potentially could be higher or lower?Q2 2024complete1Earnings transcripthighsource
Tycho, thanks for the question, and good to hear from you again. So in terms of the margin profile in the quarter, we're going through largely the impact of the transition of the vaccine-related capacity in sterile fill finish and translating into other modalities. So that's probably the biggest factor that you see there. And I think about the margin profile for our businesses, I feel good about the ability to drive strong margin expansion as we -- the top line growth comes back in certain parts of the business where we've appropriately adjusted the cost base down and where volumes have come down. And as those volumes come back, we're going to get some good pull-through that comes from that. So look forward to giving the details on '25 when we get to the January call. But yes, in terms of the margin profile and kind of the mix of business, I feel good about the ability to expand our margins.Q2 2024complete1Earnings transcripthighsource

Q3 2023
View TranscriptView SEC filing

What management said

  • "In the segment, Q3 adjusted operating income increased 21% and adjusted operating margin was 26.7%, up 290 basis points year over year."
  • "With respect to our operational performance, adjusted operating income in the quarter increased 8% and adjusted operating margin was 24.2%, 200 basis points higher than Q3 last year."
  • "In this segment, Q3 adjusted operating income increased 29% and adjusted operating margin was 16.4%, which is 340 basis points higher than Q3 2022."
  • "Q3 adjusted operating income for specialty diagnostics increased 29% in the quarter and adjusted operating margin was 26.1%, which is a 550 basis points higher than Q3 2022."
  • "Q3 adjusted operating income for life science solutions decreased 16% and adjusted operating margin was 35.9%, up 80 basis points versus the prior-year quarter."
  • "In the third quarter, our revenue was $10.57 billion, our adjusted operating income grew 8% to $2.56 billion, and we expanded our adjusted operating margin 200 basis points to 24.2%, and we delivered excellent growth in adjusted EPS, achieving a 12% increase to $5 and 69% -- $5.69 per share."
  • "So, the operating margin there was a bright spot at 16%."

What was asked

Q — Puneet Souda — Leerink Partners: Yeah. Thanks, Marc, for taking the questions. I'll wrap two of my questions into one. First, largely on M&A, given the environment right now, the type of deals that you're doing, the type of valuations you're doing at, could you maybe just give us a sense of what you're seeing out there? Obviously, Olink, prior to that, Binding Site and CorEvitas, is that the type of sort of mid-sized deals that we should continue to expect here and the opportunity base that you are seeing in M&A? And within the proteomics franchise, now with a successful Orbitrap franchise of last 15-plus years, combining that with the -- with Olink, Marc, maybe at a high level, could you provide us your, for lack of a better word, vision on proteomics despite being a sort of a tough market this year and next year?
A: Yeah. So, many thanks for the question. And so, when I think about the M&A for this year or M&A even in general, right, the criteria that we use, right, is M&A that's going to be highly valued by our customers, strengthen our strategic position, generate strong returns for our shareholders, right? And you look at what the different opportunities are and you think about in different periods of time where it's going to skew in your favor. And this year, with a more volatile macro, we've been able to add three phenomenal businesses, right, in terms of strengthening the company with incredible growth prospects, really good return profiles, right? So, that doesn't mean that next year will look exactly like this or years where you can buy companies that are really more of a balance of cost and revenue growth and those different things and different aspects of it. But this year, to be able to get The Binding Site, CorEvitas, and Olink, it's fantastic. And when I think about Olink, which this is our first opportunity, given that we had announced it during a blackout period, it's just a terrific fit, right? And you think about it's a leader in a business that has gone through that phase of being well adopted, right? So, the technology risk isn't here anymore. But it hasn't globally commercialized. It hasn't reached nearly its full potential and incredibly complementary to our leading position in mass spectrometry and proteomics. And, Puneet, thanks for reminding others about our 15-year-plus track record of Orbitrap. Astral being the next big many-year run, and the combination of AR plus Olink and the fact that we have a leading position in the life sciences instrumentation, which are very relevant in terms of qPCR for these products as well, really exciting. You know, they are a leader in their field, and we're excited to help bring that to the customer base in an accelerated fashion. And when we look to the future, you know, we expect this to be a long term, you know, mid-teens-plus growth business and be able to generate really significant, you know, adjusted operating income synergies, driven by that accelerated revenue growth. And on top of that, there's $125 million of earnings that come from the year 5 synergies, and that's going to generate double-digit returns for the shareholders. So, super exciting time, and we'll continue to be outstanding stewards of our shareholders' capital. Great. Thank you. Thanks.
Q — Eve Burstein — Bernstein: Hi there. Good morning and thanks a lot for the question. I'd love to ask about your lab products and biopharma services business unit. So, the operating margin there was a bright spot at 16%. It was higher than any point in the past. And when you talked about the puts and takes there, you called out productivity and mix as some of the positive drivers. So, just two questions there. One, on mix, if that was a positive driver, does that actually mean that sales of some of your really low-margin consumables were down? Other peer companies have talked about challenges there and brought down guidance in general lab products. So, can you talk a little bit about those dynamics? And then secondly, on productivity gains, what is driving that and are those going to be sustainable and recurring over time?
A: Yeah. So, Eve, thanks for the question. So, when I think about the margin dynamic in that segment, yeah, mix is -- it -- when you think about where the more challenging environment is in terms of customer caution and China, that impacts the lab products business, and then the wider customer caution also impacts our channel business. So, relative to the other business in that segment, that's where the mix profile comes from. In terms of productivity is about we've been rightsizing the cost base within our lab products business and given the volume change. So, that's where the majority of that is. And then just, you know, good spending wisely across the whole business. But those are probably the two main factors to call out. Thanks, Eve. Great. Thanks a lot. Operator, we have time for one more question.

What was asked

Q — Derik De Bruin — Bank of America: So, Marc, I'm just sort of curious, last quarter you were talking about 1% core growth when you were sort of looking at your initial framework for 2024. If I heard you correctly, now it's plus or minus 1%. It didn't seem like Q4 got a lot worse in anything. So what -- sort of what's changed, are you more conservative on the PPD in these businesses, are you more conservative on just tough comps, I'm just sort of curious, what's embedded now in this like more conservative outlook?
A: Stephen, why don't you -- Yes. Let me provide some context on the guidance, kind of step back on that and then -- and hopefully help frame your question. So we provided an early framing for 2024 on our last call, and we had the insight on how Q4 played out and have completed our detailed planning work with our businesses. Through that process, our view on the market outlook has not changed significant. The guidance is not significantly different from the initial framing that we provided. It includes the latest view on FX, both rates and expected mix of revenue and cost by currency. That increased revenue from our initial framing, but no impact on operating income, which reduces our margins by 20 basis points from that initial framing. And then from an operational standpoint, I think the only item of note that's changed in the past three months is a discrete item in our pharma services business. We're transitioning some of our sterile fill finish capacity from COVID vaccine support to GLP-1 support. Would have been expecting to recognize an upfront fee in Q1 2024. Now the accounting is finalized, we expect to recognize that benefit in line with production, which actually starts in 2025. So it shifted approximately $0.20 out of Q1 2024, and that's had some impact on -- in terms of the reported core growth. And then one other comment on the guidance is that we thought it best to provide a range, not a point estimate. So things are more helpful for our investors and the range of outcomes for the year. Now the range doesn't encapsulate every possible scenario for the year, but it does capture the reasonably likely scenarios of how the year can play out as we see it today. And the range is about $1 billion to a revenue and $1.05 of adjusted EPS, which I think is appropriate given the scale of the company. But hopefully, it kind of tees up kind of the framing for the guide.
Q — Vijay Kumar — Evercore ISI: Great. Thanks, Marc. And Stephen, just one quick one for you. On Q1, I think operating margin, slightly under 21%. I think the EPS is around $4.70-ish. Is that just the outsized impact from incentive comp reset, just want to understand the Q1 margin cadence?
A: Yeah. So when I think about the margin in Q1, that's definitely an element when you look at it year over year and kind of sequentially as well. So when I think about it year over year -- so there's -- obviously, we have a significant drag from the lower pandemic revenue and the reset of the incentive comp. That's just under 200 basis points in total and then about 100 basis points contribution from the core business despite the lower dollars of revenue. And the key driver there being the impact of the cost actions that we've taken over the past year. So to give you a way to frame the margin in Q1. And then yes, the margin profile grows each quarter as the revenue dollars grow during the year in terms of the profile for the year ahead. Thanks, Vijay. It's helpful. Thank you, guys. Operator we have time for one more question.

What was asked

Q — Tycho Peterson. Tycho — your line is now open: Thanks. Marc, a question on operating margins or maybe for Stephen. Lab products and services, obviously, you felt the headwinds from the vaccine and therapy roll off, but it was effectively at a two-year low. So just curious about how you think about margin for lab products going forward? And then, as we think about 2025, if TPD and Patheon can grow above the corporate average, do you still have the ability to drive 40 to 50 bps of margin expansion or potentially could be higher or lower?
A: Tycho, thanks for the question, and good to hear from you again. So in terms of the margin profile in the quarter, we're going through largely the impact of the transition of the vaccine-related capacity in sterile fill finish and translating into other modalities. So that's probably the biggest factor that you see there. And I think about the margin profile for our businesses, I feel good about the ability to drive strong margin expansion as we -- the top line growth comes back in certain parts of the business where we've appropriately adjusted the cost base down and where volumes have come down. And as those volumes come back, we're going to get some good pull-through that comes from that. So look forward to giving the details on '25 when we get to the January call. But yes, in terms of the margin profile and kind of the mix of business, I feel good about the ability to expand our margins.
